en: Abhidhānottaratantra, Chapter 37 [Tibetan & Sanskrit 40] = Lokesh Chandra facsimile edition = 1138 AD palm-leaf manuscript.
Now, therefore, I shall fully proclaim the supreme heart-mantra of the ḍākinīs.
And especially for heroes.
By the mere recollection of whom, perfect accomplishment is attained through the gradual stages.
Oṃ, to the ḍākinī of all Buddhas, Vajravarṇanī, hūṃ 2 phaṭ svāhā!
[... [142] This supreme mantra performs all rites;
it is a great mantra that grants success through mere recitation and accomplishes all desired aims.
Among the ḍākinīs and yoginīs, there are Khaṇḍarohā and likewise Lāmā.
oṃ hrīḥ ha ha hūṃ 3 phaṭ ||

This mantra is a great mantra, supreme, the performer of all rites; it is perfected through mere recitation. It is the Lord of Mantras, the Leader of Mantras, and the supreme heart of all heroes, beginning with Khaṇḍakapāla.

This is the most excellent and supreme mantra, the accomplisher of all desires and goals; it is the highest even among the higher, the unsurpassed Vīrasaṃvara. Among all heroes indeed, the mantra alone is proclaimed.
Whether in the netherworld, in heaven, or through the mantra,
whatever action proceeds within the three worlds,
the practitioner accomplishes all of that by means of the mantra.
There is nothing higher than this for the practitioner within the three worlds.
I shall speak concisely, yet without end, of the hero who is cherished by all the *ḍākinīs*.
One should visualize a divine mountain, resembling various flowers and fruits;
upon it, one should meditate on the maṇḍala of the *ḍākinīs* and the *lāmās*.
The Yoginī Khaṇḍarohā and the Vīrā; "Hā hā he he"— thus,
in the Saṃvara of the Net of the Jākinīs of the twenty-four Vīras,
all those previously mentioned, as well as the supreme Vīras and Vīrīs.
The world is pervaded by these twenty-four heroes;
likewise, the ḍākinīs of the heroes, as well as the yoginīs and lāmās,
and Khaṇḍarohā and others, are to be visualized by practitioners in all rites within the locations of the maṇḍala.

One who desires accomplishment, being well-composed, should constantly worship those situated within the wheel according to the previously mentioned procedure. One should sacrifice in the *Ḍākinījālasamvara*,
the great wheel that is the abode of all accomplishments.
The well-spoken words of ten million Buddhas and ten million Heroes are present;
for each individual Hero, there is a retinue numbering ten million Vīra-Ḍākinīs,
and likewise for the Yoginīs and Lāmās.
Khaṇḍarohā, in particular, is auspicious and bestows all accomplishments.
The fortieth chapter, on the non-duality of the hearts of the ḍākinīs and heroes, from the *Abhidhānottarottara*.
